name: Theme Building
by: Pereira & Luckman (William Pereira and Charles Luckman), with Paul Williams and Welton Becket
key_features: White form like a flying saucer landed on four legs; dedicated June 1961.

name: Tramway Gas Station
by: Albert Frey and Robson C. Chambers
key_features: Cantilevered wedge-shaped canopy called a hyperbolic paraboloid; now a visitor center.

name: Wayfarers Chapel
key_features: Glass enclosure lets the surrounding landscape define the sacred space; on a bluff above the Pacific.

name: Koerner House
key_features: Post-and-beam frame, shed roof, wide eaves and large glass walls with sliding doors.

name: Reunion Tower
key_features: 561 ft observation tower topped by a sphere with an aluminum-strut geodesic dome.

name: Freeway Park
key_features: Built over Interstate 5 and a parking lot; blends brutalist architecture with greenery.

name: Tacoma Dome
key_features: 530 ft diameter, 152 ft high; largest wooden-domed arena by volume when opened.

name: Tempe Municipal Building
by: Rolf Osland, Michael Goodwin, and Kemper Goodwin
key_features: Inverted-pyramid city hall; the shape is credited with keeping it cool in summer and warm in winter.

name: Solar Building
key_features: World's first commercial building heated primarily by solar energy; 56 collectors on a south-facing wall.

name: Fort Worth Water Gardens
key_features: Active Pool sends water down 38 ft of terraces; Quiet Pool walls are covered in thin sheets of water.

name: Nasher Sculpture Center
key_features: Glass roof over galleries; garden terraces down to an open-air auditorium.

name: Dee and Charles Wyly Theatre
by: Joshua Prince-Ramus and Rem Koolhaas (REX | OMA)
key_features: Stacked vertical theatre; facade of anodized aluminium rods symbolising theatre curtain folds.

name: Oregon Convention Center
key_features: Twin spire towers bring light inside; ballroom of 35,000 sq ft is Portland's largest.

name: Norton Simon Museum
by: Thornton Ladd and John Kelsey (Ladd & Kelsey)
key_features: Facade faced with 115,000 glazed tiles by Edith Heath on an undulating surface.

name: Jacobs Medical Center
key_features: Tower of 509,500 sq ft with 245 beds; surgery pavilion has 14 operating rooms.

name: MacMillan Bloedel Building
key_features: 27-storey head office conceived by Arthur Erickson in 1965; opened 13 December 1968.

name: Lester B. Pearson Building
key_features: Office building at 125 Sussex Drive, headquarters of Global Affairs Canada; opened 1 August 1973.

name: Théâtre Maisonneuve
key_features: 1,453-seat theatre in the Place des Arts complex, inaugurated 1967.

name: Roy Thomson Hall
key_features: Circular concert hall with a sloping, curvilinear glass exterior; opened 1982.

name: Grande Bibliothèque
key_features: Quebec's national library in downtown Montréal, opened 30 April 2005.

name: Our Lady of Victory Church (Igloo Church)
key_features: Igloo-shaped Catholic church in Inuvik, opened and consecrated 1960 after two years of construction.

name: Peace Bridge
key_features: Pedestrian and cycle bridge over the Bow River, opened 24 March 2012.

name: Monumento a la Revolución
key_features: 67 m memorial arch, the tallest triumphal arch in the world; built 1910–1938.

name: Torre del Reformador
key_features: 71.85 m steel-framework tower resembling the Eiffel Tower, built 1935 for the centenary of Justo Rufino Barrios.

name: Hotel Nacional de Cuba
key_features: Spanish eclectic hotel on Taganana Hill with views over the sea; opened 1930.

name: Gran Teatro de La Habana
key_features: Home of the Cuban National Ballet on the Paseo del Prado, designed by Belgian architect Paul Belau.

name: Saint Joseph's Oratory
by: Dalbé Viau, Alphonse Venne, Lucien Parent, Dom Paul Bellot
key_features: Canada's largest church, with one of the largest church domes in the world; completed 1967.

name: Old City Hall
key_features: Romanesque-style civic building; home of Toronto City Council from 1899 to 1966.

name: William G. Davis Building
key_features: Brutalist single mega-structure above the Credit River valley, completed 1973 as the South Building.

name: Plaza de las Tres Culturas
key_features: Square in Tlatelolco joining pre-Columbian, colonial and modern buildings; completed 1966.

name: National Theatre of Panama
key_features: Italian operetta-style theatre in the old city, opened 1 October 1908.

name: Groninger Museum
by: Alessandro Mendini, Philippe Starck, Coop Himmelb(l)au
key_features: Pavilions by Starck (silver cylinder), Mendini (yellow tower) and Coop Himmelb(l)au (pale blue deconstructivist space).

name: Erasmus Bridge
key_features: 802 m cable-stayed and bascule bridge; Ben van Berkel's design has one backward-leaning pylon.

name: Het Nieuwe Instituut
key_features: Archive, exhibition spaces and Sonneveld House set around a pond and small park; opened 1993.

name: Timmerhuis
key_features: OMA's contemporary building combined with J.R.A. Koops's post-war reconstruction architecture of 1950-53.

name: Royal Palace of Amsterdam
key_features: Built as Amsterdam's city hall on 13,659 wooden piles; Van Campen took charge of the design in 1648.

name: Europa building
by: Philippe Samyn and Partners, with Studio Valle (Michel Polak's Résidence Palace)
key_features: Lantern-shaped multi-storey meeting-room block joined to the listed 1920s Art Deco Résidence Palace façade.

name: Flagey Building (Radio House)
key_features: Streamline Moderne 'ocean liner' style; twelve recording studios sit in two acoustic towers. Won by competition.

name: Royal Greenhouses of Laeken
by: Alphonse Balat (later Henri Maquet, Charles Girault)
key_features: Heated greenhouses built 1874-1905 for Leopold II, including the domed 'Iron Church' greenhouse.

name: M – Museum Leuven
key_features: Beel's design joins historical features and sleek contemporary architecture around a courtyard.

name: Leuven Town Hall
by: Sulpitius van Vorst, Jan Keldermans II, Matheus de Layens
key_features: Late-Gothic, built 1439-69: lace-like ornament, a steep roof with four tiers of dormers and octagonal corner turrets.

name: Royal Museum for Central Africa (AfricaMuseum)
by: Charles Girault (2018 renovation: Stéphane Beel Architects)
key_features: Neoclassical 'palace' reminiscent of the Petit Palais, with large gardens extending into the Tervuren Forest.

name: Grand Théâtre de Luxembourg
key_features: Won by competition in 1958; its distinctive 1960s architecture was kept through the 2002-03 renovation.

name: Eye Filmmuseum
key_features: Building on the IJ waterfront holding two gallery spaces and four cinemas; opened 2012.

name: Saint-Cyr House
key_features: Only 4 m wide but very tall; polychrome brick façade with wrought iron that mimics vegetation.

name: Villa Empain
key_features: Art Deco villa of 1930-34: polished granite façades, an enclosed courtyard and a swimming pool.

name: Olympic Stadium (Olympisch Stadion)
key_features: Amsterdam School stadium whose design won the 1928 Olympic gold medal in architecture; second ring added 1937.

name: Silodam
key_features: Housing and mixed-use complex on a former breakwater beside the 1890s Stone Silo; 95 homes in a container-like stack.

name: OBA Central Library (Oosterdok)
key_features: Ten-floor, 28,500 m² central library beside Amsterdam Centraal, with a restaurant terrace on the seventh floor.

name: Kamzík TV Tower
by: Stanislav Májek, Jakub Tomašák, Juraj Kozák, Milan Jurica, Ján Privitzer
key_features: Transmission tower on Kamzík hill, built in 1975 to replace an earlier mast; designed by a team of five architects.

name: Puskás Aréna
key_features: National stadium by György Skardelli on the site of the old Puskás stadium; built 2017–19, opened with Hungary–Uruguay.

name: Tallinn TV Tower
key_features: 313 m tower of 50 cm reinforced-concrete rings built for the 1980 Olympic regatta; observation deck at 170 m.

name: Grand Hotel Prishtina
by: Bashkim Fehmiu, Dragan Kovačević, Miša Jevremović
key_features: 13-storey, 350-room hotel built 1974–78; designed by Bashkim Fehmiu with two Belgrade architects.

name: Zetra Olympic Hall (Juan Antonio Samaranch Olympic Hall)
key_features: Angular hall with a copper roof, built 1981–82 for the 1984 Winter Olympics; rebuilt after the war and finished in 1999.

name: Stari Most (Old Bridge)
key_features: Single-arch stone Ottoman bridge by Mimar Hayruddin, a student of Sinan; rebuilt and reopened on 23 July 2004.

name: Kadinjača Memorial Complex
key_features: Memorial complex built 1952–79; the 1979 expansion by Živković and Đokić gave its present form.

name: Seimas Palace
key_features: Parliament complex with a square-plan main building by the Nasvytis brothers; first part done 1980.

name: Monument to the Revolution of the People of Moslavina
key_features: About 10 m high, 20 m long: a stylised sun with two asymmetric wings, inspired by Nike, set in the landscape.

name: Park-Monument of the Bulgarian-Soviet Friendship
by: Kamen Goranov (with sculptors Evgeni Barumov, Alyosha Kafedzhiyski)
key_features: Concrete memorial 23 m high and 48 m wide, reached by a 301-step 'Staircase of Victory'; built 1974–78.

name: Telephone Palace (SART building)
key_features: First major modernist building on Calea Victoriei: a steel-skeleton tower built 1931–33 and inaugurated in 1934.

name: Palace of Culture, Iași
key_features: Flamboyant Neo-Gothic palace on the old Princely Court site, built with modern materials; completed 1925.

name: Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge
key_features: 179.5 m stone bridge over the Drina, completed 1577 by Sinan for the Grand Vizier Mehmed Paša Sokolović; UNESCO-listed.

name: Peleș Castle
key_features: Neo-Renaissance alpine palace by Johannes Schultz; Karel Liman added the towers, incl. the 66 m main tower.

name: Hungarian State Opera House
key_features: Opera house on Andrássy Avenue designed by Miklós Ybl; construction began 1875, opened 27 September 1884.

name: Grand Hotel International Prague
key_features: Socialist-realist tower hotel built 1952–56 as a military hotel; much original interior artwork survives.

name: Praha hlavní nádraží (Prague Main Station)
key_features: Art Nouveau station by Josef Fanta, 1901–09; steel train hall by Marjanko and Kornfeld, 1905–06.

name: Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque (Blue Mosque)
key_features: Large blue and silver dome with four minarets, one at each corner.

name: Palace of Justice, Putrajaya
by: AR Ahmad Rozi A Wahab (aQidea Architect)
key_features: Blends Islamic, Moorish and Palladian influences round a large central rotunda that organises the rooms.

name: Stadium Merdeka
key_features: Partly sunken amphitheatre under shell roofs that were the world's largest cantilever shells at completion.

name: Sala Chalermkrung Royal Theatre
key_features: Modernist cinema-theatre with a neon-lit front facade billed as the largest in Asia.

name: Ho Chi Minh City Hall
key_features: Central clock tower inspired by Paris's town hall; Corinthian columns, Renaissance, Baroque and Beaux-Arts styling.

name: Saigon Opera House
key_features: Flamboyant Third Republic style, with a facade modelled on the Petit Palais in Paris.

name: Hanoi Opera House
by: François Lagisquet, Broyer and Victorin Harlay
key_features: Neoclassical with French Renaissance elements, modelled on the Palais Garnier but smaller, in locally suited materials.

name: Vietnam Museum of Ethnology
by: Ha Duc Linh (exhibition building); Véronique Dollfus (interiors)
key_features: Main exhibition building shaped like a Dong Son drum; the second building, opened 2013, is kite-shaped.

name: Hotel Indonesia
key_features: International Style hotel of a 16-storey Ramayana Wing and an 8-storey Ganesha Wing.

name: Gedung Sate
key_features: Neoclassical with Hindu-Buddhist motifs; central pinnacle shaped like a satay skewer with six spheres.

name: Savoy Homann Hotel
key_features: Curved, streamlined Art Deco exterior and interior.

name: Jakarta Cathedral
key_features: Neo-Gothic cruciform plan with three spires, including two 60 m towers at the entrance.

name: Manila Central Post Office
by: Juan M. Arellano, Tomás Mapúa and Ralph Doane
key_features: Neoclassical; 16 Ionic pillars above the entrance steps, recessed attic storey, two semi-circular wings.

name: Manila Hotel
key_features: California mission style with an H-shaped plan, giving well-ventilated rooms on two wings with harbour views.

name: University of Santo Tomas Main Building
key_features: Built as 40 independent structures linked by pre-cast flooring, round two interior courtyards, on an 86 x 74 m plan.

name: Manila Cathedral
key_features: Latin-cross plan with a Neo-Romanesque facade replicating that of the previous cathedral.

name: Singapore Indoor Stadium
by: Kenzo Tange with Raglan Squire & Partners
key_features: Cone-shaped roof over a pillarless arena.

name: Supreme Court of Singapore
key_features: Disc-shaped Court of Appeal on the ninth storey, and extensive glass atria and skylights meant to signify transparency.

name: Ipoh Railway Station
key_features: Large central dome over the porte-cochere and deep open-air loggias on the ground and upper floors.

name: Jakarta Kota Station
key_features: Barrel-vault roof over the entrance and hall; Art Deco blended with local traditional forms.

name: Sultan Mosque
key_features: Two gold onion domes decorated with glass bottle ends, and two eight-storey minarets on the east facade.

name: Wat Rong Khun (White Temple)
key_features: All-white ubosot set with mirrored glass fragments that sparkle; bridge lined with outstretched hands.

name: Inland Steel Building
by: Bruce Graham & Walter Netsch (Skidmore, Owings & Merrill)
key_features: 332-foot International Style tower, one of the first Loop skyscrapers after World War II.

name: John C. Kluczynski Federal Building
key_features: 45-storey tower completing the Federal Center, with Mies's post office and plaza.

name: Reliance Building
key_features: The first skyscraper with large plate-glass windows over most of its surface.

name: Richard J. Daley Center
key_features: Modernist courthouse tower beside an open granite plaza used for gatherings.

name: Rookery Building
key_features: Considered the oldest standing high-rise in Chicago; load-bearing exterior walls.

name: North Christian Church
key_features: 192-foot-tall church with interiors by Alexander Girard and landscape by Dan Kiley.

name: Sarasota High School
key_features: Public high school by Paul Rudolph, built 1958–59.

name: Graycliff
key_features: Summer estate on a bluff above Lake Erie, designed 1926 and built 1926–31.

name: Herbert and Katherine Jacobs First House
key_features: Single-storey, L-shaped, 1,550 sq ft house, sometimes cited as Wright's first Usonian.

name: Pope–Leighey House
key_features: Wright house moved twice; now on the grounds of Woodlawn Plantation.

name: Home Federal Savings and Loan Building
key_features: One of the first steel-and-glass modernist buildings downtown; now the Catholic Pastoral Center.

name: National Farmers' Bank of Owatonna
key_features: Historic bank by Louis Sullivan with decorative elements by George Elmslie.
